parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim from Claim 3.2. The notation π(s) is defined only for finite prime sets, and the premises given (T meets every t ∈ C, hence every supp(a_i)) do not force T to be finite; the text nowhere proves that minimal transversals of C are finite. The objector's family C={{2,x_n}} shows an intersecting antichain of finite sets can have an infinite minimal transversal {x_n : n≥1} (deleting x_k leaves {2,x_k} unhit), so finiteness is not automatic from (i)+(ii). Hence hypothesis (iii) of the Step 4 Theorem is verified only for finite minimal transversals. This is load-bearing: in Step 4(c) the transversal I ∪ Z_ω is infinite and Zorn yields a possibly infinite minimal T, whose membership in C (and finiteness, used in 'Since T is finite...') is exactly what is unproved. The finiteness obligation therefore fails as written.
